about: A Guide-style short on Wang Bi (the user, 2026-09-30: "can you help come up with a Wang Bi 'hitchhikers guide to the universe' style short? that might be fun."). A handheld book-device shows its entry on the I Ching in flat, cheerful animation; a narrator reads it dry. Our own device and lines: no DON'T PANIC, towels or Guide logo. Draft 2: Astra's revision (docs/research/2026-09-30-codex-guide-wangbi.md), ~93 words, ~40 s of speech.

voice.name: hitchiker's guide v1
voice.note: Designed by the user with ElevenLabs Voice Design, 2026-09-30, from a description of the register (a dry English reference-book reader), naming no one; the user on its first takes: 'love it.' Our own voice, so Astra's Attenborough concern about David no longer applies. Direction: plain, even pace; short pauses; no wonder or reverence, no emphasis announcing the jokes.

previous.name: David
previous.note: Picked by the user 2026-09-30 (https://elevenlabs.io/voices/WdZjiN0nNcik2LBjOHiv): 'a classic nature narrator'. A synthetic voice: this short carries the AI-content label on YouTube and TikTok. Astra advises another voice: this one's marketing ('David', 'national treasure', 'classic nature narrator') invites an Attenborough comparison, and he objected publicly to AI copies of his voice in November 2024. The founder's call. Direction either way: plain, even pace; short pauses; no wonder or reverence, no emphasis announcing the jokes. The founder, 2026-09-30, after Astra's advice: 'Lets keep David for now.' Takes need a paid ElevenLabs plan: the API refuses library voices on the free plan (402 paid_plan_required), and free output has no commercial licence. His takes: series/renders/voice/guide-wangbi-WdZjiN0nNcik2LBjOHiv.json.

narration.text: The I-Ching. Sixty-four situations, with roots about three thousand years old.
narration.picture: The device lights up: THE I-CHING. Sixty-four hexagrams tile in.
narration.source: history; the Ten Wings are later (Stanford Encyclopedia, 'Chinese Philosophy of Change')

narration.text: For centuries, people consulted it about the future.
narration.picture: A tiny figure sorts and counts yarrow stalks; a question mark floats up.

narration.text: Wang Bi offered some reading instructions.
narration.picture: A small flat scholar, arms folded. WANG BI 王弼, 226–249.
narration.source: Sanguozhi 28, Pei Songzhi's note (He Shao's biography)

narration.text: He died young. His commentary became a standard for centuries.
narration.picture: A candle burns down beside a growing stack of pages.
narration.source: Zhouyi zhu; Kong Yingda's Zhouyi zhengyi (642) is built on it. Sanguozhi gives his age as 24 (traditional reckoning), so no number is spoken

narration.text: Grasp the meaning. Then forget the image.
narration.picture: The device opens an image gallery: a dragon, a horse, a cart losing its spokes (hexagram 9, kept apart from Qian's entry). On screen: 得意忘象 grasp the meaning, forget the image.
narration.source: Zhouyi lüeli, Ming xiang: 得意而忘象

narration.text: Borrowing from Zhuangzi: an image is a fish trap. Catch the fish; put down the trap.
narration.picture: A wicker trap, a fish; the fish is lifted out, the trap set aside. On screen: 筌 fish trap.
narration.source: Zhouyi lüeli, Ming xiang: 象者，意之筌也; Zhuangzi 26 (words and meaning)

narration.text: If the meaning is strength, why insist on a horse?
narration.picture: The horse fades; the word STRENGTH stays.
narration.source: Zhouyi lüeli, Ming xiang: 義苟在健，何必馬乎

narration.text: Six Lines reads it for judgment: what makes sense to do here.
narration.picture: The tiny figure from before, now at a fork in a road, thinking.

narration.text: Recommended for: making decisions. Not recommended for: finding out what happens next.
narration.picture: The entry's footer, typed. Then the ivory close with sixlines.day.

onScreenChinese: 得意忘象 grasp the meaning, forget the image

timing.note: lead: the device switches on before the first line; gap: silence between lines; tail: hold after the last.

spelling: I-Ching, hyphenated, in this short's narration and on screen (the user, 2026-09-30: 'can we use I-Ching instead of I Ching').
